what_it_does: This paper describes a specialized memory chip for AI edge devices that performs computation while storing data (called CIM, Computing-In-Memory). The challenge: CIM typically supports either integer math (efficient but less accurate) or floating-point math (accurate but wasteful on power). New microscaling formats (MX, a hybrid numeric format) split numbers into exponent and mantissa parts, balancing accuracy and efficiency. But existing CIM designs aren't built for multiple formats. This 16nm chip supports integer, floating-point, and microscaling formats all in one 216KB memory macro. It includes a multi-mode input processor that handles format conversion inside the CIM itself, a hybrid adder tree that avoids redundant operations common to MX format, and adaptive data flows that reconfigure how results accumulate based on the active format. Achieves 188 TOPS per watt (tera-operations per second per watt) in integer mode and 133.5 TFLOPS per watt (tera-floating-operations per second per watt) in floating-point.
